facts.text: Wenona sprang to life in 1852 when the Illinois Central Railroad built its first freight depot, passenger station, and rail‑men housing.
The town’s boom came from a coal mine opened in 1882 that once employed 550 miners and paid wages in gold coin.
In 1958, a radar station was erected atop the old mine’s slag pile to spot incoming missiles aimed at Chicago or Milwaukee.
The Wenona Coal Mine Historical Site was officially dedicated on August 10, 2018, during the town’s Wenona Days celebration.
Wenona Days, the town’s annual festival, offers live music, food trucks, a rock climbing wall, and other family‑friendly activities.
Wenona straddles Marshall and LaSalle counties, placing it within both the Peoria Metropolitan and Ottawa Micropolitan statistical areas.
